I remember the gate shut. I remember the road hidden. I remember the soldiers entering. I will not tell you those were one man's act.
The copies survive. I will keep them. Some people said no when I asked them to stand beside me. Their answer stays no.
Then begin with your own hands. Do not fill the empty places with another person's vow.
Make the account public and I will leave its judgment with you. Release me quietly and preserve the record without opening every private memory.
Or carry the unresolved binding yourself. Or destroy me and lose what no copy holds.
Whatever I choose, the order stays in the book. Families still need a road home. Edric still has to answer.
The kitchen is working. There is a route and a dry refuge. We have tried the shifts, not just written them down.
Then there are two more things you may attempt. Share stewardship only with the keepers who still freely offer it. An empty place remains empty until somebody chooses it.
And if we leave?
Carry the people and their human records through the prepared passage. Undo this boundary, and its shelter will not follow. Neither will the complete account I hold.
A rota can fail. A refuge can fail. Neither makes the old choices disappear.
Then choose whose work begins when mine ends.
There are spaces beside the names now. For the next shift, and for anyone who needs to stop.
Who fills a space when somebody leaves?
Someone who offers. We ask. We wait. If nobody can, we write that the work is uncovered.
The Hart did not make the work smaller.
No. It can no longer make one person carry it in silence.
A hinge, a rail, and the kitchen latch. Those are the jobs. Nobody promised the iron would stop wearing out.
The rota leaves a gap for weather. Sensible. Weather has never signed anything I gave it.
And if a keeper withdraws?
We close the unsafe part until somebody can do it. A promise is not a brace.
Your shift is still on the board. Unless you have something to tell the board.
The passage is open. The watch still changes at the posted hour.
Some people stayed. Some went on. Their shares were packed either way.
Do the keepers agree about everything?
They agree about the next handover. Tomorrow we may have to talk again.
Then we keep the empty places visible.
And we ask before writing a name in one.
The orders, the signatures and the accounts we recovered are packed. These are human records. They remain evidence.
What is missing?
What only the Hart remembered. We cannot fill that absence by guessing.
Leave the notice where someone returning can find it.
A road to the record. Not a claim that we carried everything.
Dry tools underneath. Sleeping cloths on top. Nobody should have to unpack a whole cart to lie down.
I would prefer a lighter future. This one has cooking pots.
What stays?
The walls. What we cannot carry. The people who freely chose another road know where we are going.
The pots have arrived. Tomorrow somebody still has to cook.
The refuge has beds. It has no oath around it. We keep watch with people now.
Can the road remain open behind us?
While we maintain it. Whoever comes later deserves to know both where it goes and what it costs.
And the Hart?
We chose to leave its shelter and its full account. Keep the copies dry. Do not call them the whole of what we lost.
Count the portions, not the mouths into debts. A person can eat here and still disagree with us afterward.
People keep bringing me empty bowls as if I can fill them with a speech. Give me a table that stays upright. I can begin there.
A common fire saves wood. Carrying shares home saves arguments. I can tell you what either costs; I cannot tell every household which cost to bear.
A beam can look straight and still have a rotten seat. Hold it while I check the bearing. We are building for the cart after ours, too.
The water is slow here until the mill lets a pulse through. Read the wet marks on both banks before you promise anyone a quick crossing.
Mark where a load can wait safely. A route is not open just because someone brave enough can get through it.
A bed should not become another confessional. Let the person sleep first. If they want to tell us anything tomorrow, tomorrow has room for it.
Keep the dressings where a stranger can find them. If only I know where they are, we have built a room that stops working whenever I am tired.

lines.text: Have you tried again?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: I chop onions now. Nessa tastes it, and I try to leave the spoon alone.

lines.text: Do you always explain why you lost?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Only when the explanation is more interesting than the game.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: And when it isn't?

lines.text: Then I improve it. The light is usually at fault.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: You could just say I played well.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: You played well. There. An exhausting afternoon's honesty. Shall we have another?

lines.text: Do you ever run out of things to say?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Frequently. I keep three old stories ready so nobody notices.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: I notice the one about the shortcut.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Everyone notices that one. It's still quicker than admitting I'm tired.

lines.text: You can be tired here.

lines.text: Good. Sit where you can watch the door. I would like to stop doing it for a little while.

lines.text: Are all the flowers you keep useful?

lines.text: The yellow ones are dreadful medicine. Very cheerful, though.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: You planted them for the color?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Yes. Toma calls them weeds with ambition. I like them better for it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Will they stay?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: As long as they leave room for the roots I need. I can want two things in one garden.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: What do you read when the weather keeps you indoors?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Travel accounts. Especially the ones written by people who plainly got lost.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: For the descriptions?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: For the corrections. You can hear them getting less certain as the pages go on.

lines.text: Would you make the journeys yourself?

lines.text: One or two. Somewhere with a warm room at the end, preferably. I'm quite adventurous about warm rooms.

lines.text: Have you ever made something just because you liked its shape?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: A little iron bird. Very poor at being a hook.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Was it meant to be a hook?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: That is what I told people. It was meant to be a bird.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Do you still have it?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Somewhere safe. I might try another. The wings were better than the feet.

lines.text: What sort of blue?

lines.text: Dark enough to look green when the light goes. I saw it once on a traveler's sleeve.

lines.text: What makes a good visitor?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: You could try the question again.

lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: I sit. I notice the bowls from there as well.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Perhaps they want your company.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: That is what Elna said. Quite sharply, in fact. I had a lovely evening once I believed her.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Where would you go with an empty cart?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Somewhere I had never been asked to take a cart. A difficult destination to put on a map.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Sea or hills?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Hills. I would like to reach the top and have nothing to unload.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Have you chosen a route?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: I'm keeping that part for myself a while. Planning it has been pleasant.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: What do your crew argue about when the road is easy?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Where to put a wet cup. It is an argument of surprising endurance.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Where do you put yours?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: On top of whatever is least likely to fall. Apparently that is not a system.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Do you settle it as their leader?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: They have put a small cloth beside my seat. I have decided to regard it as a treaty.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.text: Mind the hot side. A loaf looks much the same before it burns your hand.
The one I told you to mind. There is water by the care bench, if Anwen needs a hand.
The cups are identical.
And a finish to the shift?
These tools are for the new work, then.
Stand on the pale stone. Not because it is lucky. Because it is firm.
Only the ones I want to reach the other side. So far, everyone.
If that is another wager, carry the water first.
The kettle stays here this time.
Your left or the wagon's?
No daylight through the cover.
Heavy end down first. No, the other heavy end. They never put a light one on these carts.
With the wheel, yes. Not with finding advice. I have enough of that.
Last one on firm ground. I counted people before crates this time too.
You did. That was the job, and it is finished. Help me dry the rope before we discuss the next one.
You can count the shares. I'll cut them.
From your thumb on the scale. Sit down, Rook. There is a share for you too.
Then I can count what stays dry, not what the rain leaves me.
The kitchen needs the answer before tomorrow, not a number to wait behind.
Then put the hungry people on the page too.
I intend to. And I'll bring the empty bowls back before you close the book.
I need a rack that doesn't leave the bottom sack in the wet.
I have asked. He says the ground needs an opinion too.
We moved the sound boards off the damp. That much we can do today.
Still work, not a promise you have to make for us.
The rebuilding account reached us. I can plan the next load around what is actually there.
No. Something useful, with its costs written down.
Walk the dry approach with me. We check before anyone steps onto the crossing.
Feel for the loose turn. No load on it yet.
Good. Now it is a checked rope, not a brave prediction.
The tune can finish before the washing starts.
I haven't mentioned the second bucket.
I was about to find another job. You caught me.
I can leave if you want the quiet.
Stay. Tell me the least important thing you saw on the road.
A crow trying to carry a twig through a gap too narrow for it.
Did it turn the twig?
Eventually. It seemed annoyed that this worked.
There was a splendid ending to this story. I put it somewhere between the second inn and the third.
Start with the ending you have.
A man bought a hat. No, the hat was important earlier.
Perhaps he was pleased with it.
You have reduced a triumph of storytelling to a satisfactory purchase.
I am pleased for him.
Yellow, I think. I am allowed to change my mind before you answer.
What are we choosing?
The color I would paint a door if I had a free afternoon.
Yellow would be easy to find in the rain.
That is useful, but I was enjoying how cheerful it would look.
Then yellow. Cheerful first.
Tell me where you would put your thumb. I'll keep my hands here.
Away from the head of the tool.
Good. And your other hand?
Clear of where it comes down.
There. I managed an entire lesson without grabbing anything.
You moved your elbow twice.
Go on. You have the expression you get before a careful question.
Would you rather have a sunny room or a cool one?
Sunny. I can always open a window. That was a good question.
I had two more prepared.
Save them. We can manage a conversation without provisions for the whole week.
Sunny, then.
Do you think it will rain before morning?
I was going to ask you.
That is inconvenient. I had hoped to borrow your certainty.
We could look again before we leave.
Or admit we don't know and get indoors while it is dry.
I prefer that answer.
Move over. I mean—would you mind moving over?
There is room here.
I heard myself. You needn't pretend the first part was courteous.
You asked again.
It takes longer than I expected.
We have time for a question.
I tried practicing with the door open once. Nobody came nearer.
That is a review of sorts.
An unusually unanimous one. I had to laugh before I could close the door.
Did it help the playing?
Not at all. It helped the practice.
Then you had an audience after all.
I wrote three lines this morning and crossed out two.
Are you keeping the third?
For now. It sounds rather pleased with itself.
Must you correct that too?
Perhaps tomorrow. I wanted to tell somebody I had written it.
I am glad you told me.
I have nearly said 'while you wait' three times. You aren't waiting for anything, are you?
No.
Then I can finish this without finding a form for you.
You can.
That was still warm. I had forgotten it could be.
You might try again tomorrow.
I am trying very hard not to ask whether you've eaten.
I have. You may sit without feeding me.
Good. Now I need something else to say.
Tell me about the badger.
An excellent piece of carving. Slightly round. Fierce in the right light.
I look forward to meeting it.
Nothing needs checking for a moment. I have checked that quite thoroughly.
What happens now?
We stand here without discussing the crossing.
The wind has changed.
So it has. That can be the whole conversation if we like.
I would like that.
Hot side of the tray. Other side of the argument.
The small loaf is not a shortage. It's the one I dropped. There, a trade secret.
Set out another bowl. Worry does less harm with something to do.
Weigh before you divide. Generosity that forgets the last household isn't generous.
No one burned? Then give me room and we'll survive it.
A moment between jobs.
Check the strap before leaning on the cart.
The cart has fewer opinions than the crew. More reliable brakes, too.
You can take the next useful job. That's enough for now.
The load is tied to survive a turn, not to look tidy while standing still.
Keep the approach clear. People need a way through.
A moment between jobs.
I'll split it between the two still working. This short knot is spare; pull the turns apart when you want to learn how it holds.
No one has to give testimony for a meal. Keep the empty delivery sleeve; the names inside are mine to protect.
Nessa has heard that every delayed load went into the old mill. Her own missing delivery does not prove that.
The next batch needs water. Bread takes its time, however loudly people ask for it.
I marked that load already. Check the tag before you move it.
Stop where it is firm. You can ask me from there.
A notch for daylight, a hood for night. Neither replaces looking where you step.
The captain is answering for his orders. I am still checking the crossing.
Senn has gone. The rope still needs checking before anyone crosses.
Removing the captain did not mend a single board. Keep this approach clear.
Read the answer before you bring me another seal.
Leave room for the tray. People still have to eat while the great hall talks.
Hold that wheel, would you? The patient has had enough surprises for one journey.
You can sit here. It is a seat, Kael. We needn't decide anything larger over supper.
I can bake less. I cannot tell a child a smaller loaf is the same size.
There you are. Sit down a moment; I can talk without stopping the bread.
I closed the crossing. I can tell you why. I cannot tell you they all got home.
Firm ground this side. Catch your breath before you tell me what happened.
I know you. You were on our escort. You left at the bend.
I learned to set a wheel after that. We still needed to get somewhere.
No. Follow the work line if you mean to help now. Toma knows where it crosses the old road. Do not tell me what I must want from you.
Light crate to the left. Heavy one stays low. Tor says the frame will hold if someone seats that brace.
There was no one left to do it for us. Mind your fingers.
Outside the load. Nobody proves anything by standing under a falling crate.
All here. People first, then crates.
That is what I asked. It does not change the other road.
Good. Help me get the rope dry.
Keep what I gave you. Not a list of everyone who was there. Some of them do not want you finding them.
Start with your own name, Kael. Mine is not the price of putting it there.
The bread can stay by the gate. I am not ready to sit with you tonight.
Thank you. That is all I asked. The next load leaves when I have chosen the route.
Nessa packed too much bread. She says that is a problem for my judgment, not her baking.
I am still choosing. You needn't wait beside the door until I do.
A seat, then. Nothing larger over supper.
Nessa brushes flour off the counter. 'Yesterday that sack made twelve. Today it made nine. Same seam, same oven. Tell me which of those has learned to lie.'
A traveler: 'We heard the bell stopped. We didn't know if that meant the road was welcome.'
Nera keeps her eyes on the post. 'I cut it. The rope was pulling me in. I wrote that the crossing failed. I did not write about my knife.'
You corrected your own account. Mine says what I gave it, and no more. There is still a load to hand over after your business in the glade.
All of us crossed. That matters. It is not the same as having come back for us then.
I have a crew to think about. Ask me about the work we are doing now, Kael. The old road is not going anywhere.

Nera accepted company for the handover and kept her own plans. Kael completed the existing journey home; the next road is an offer, not proof of forgiveness.

Nera: 'The next route is mine to choose. Supper can just be supper.'

Nera kept a little distance while the relief work was handed over. Kael respected it and completed the existing homecoming. Cooperation did not erase the abandoned escort.

Nera: 'The next route is mine to choose. We can work together without sharing the rest.'
Heavy sacks over this wheel. One at a time. ... Kael? I remember you. Not now. Help Anwen find her missing people. This load is my business.
Easy. Pulling only tightens it. I'll stay here a moment.
There you are.
I wasn't ready to promise you a road. I haven't forgotten you.
Bracken. A better name than whatever they scratched off that harness.
The road isn't kind. Neither is being left on it. You needn't decide as quickly as I do.
Just the buckle. Keep still. Then the choice is yours.
The grain is no longer being held against a signature. Keeping it moving will take more than words.
Hunger does not make an oath freely given.
They have not taken it down. Somebody is afraid enough to cover it and kind enough to keep it dry.
A private account can still invite a second witness.
Keeping the token is not the same as keeping them safe.
Mind the cup on the step. The man from the south road needs it more than I need a clean floor.
Three people missing?
Bram drove. Sella had Oren beside her. He left his coat here because the sun was out.
Take the north road into Wychwood. Look for their cart, then bring me what you find. They have people waiting here.
They found old wooden tokens where the road was being repaired. Sella asked me to read one. I did.
What happened when you read it?
The candles went out. I sent them away while I found a rite I thought would keep them safe.
If you find red thread around black feathers, keep it intact. I tied it. I owe you that much before you go.
Thank you for the water. Now, the three who have not come home.
Three people missing?
Bram drove. Sella had Oren beside her. He left his coat here because the sun was out.
Take the north road into Wychwood. Look for their cart, then bring me what you find. They have people waiting here.
They found old wooden tokens where the road was being repaired. Sella asked me to read one. I did.
What happened when you read it?
The candles went out. I sent them away while I found a rite I thought would keep them safe.
If you find red thread around black feathers, keep it intact. I tied it. I owe you that much before you go.
I have put the grain list beside the burial book. No one has to sign one to receive the other.
I could call that a beginning. It is mostly a table and two people willing to sit at it.
Beginnings usually look smaller when somebody is doing the work.
I will give you the register. You said you would not demand my oath. I am still not agreeing to stand in the rite.
The record can speak to facts. It cannot make your promise for you.
Then you do understand the difference.
Edric wants my hand on the new seal. He has already counted the households that cannot afford to refuse.
The old rite borrowed consent from frightened people. That is why it keeps breaking.
Can the Hart be released without making everyone here swear?
Yes. Someone must freely keep the recovered account. One person can begin. More people can share the work.
Three strokes. A burial, a restored name, and a promise that has stopped holding.
I cut the rope last winter. A novice heard an erased name and walked into the sealed chapel. I found him too late.
You closed it again.
Yes. I told myself I was buying time. The graves will show what that time cost.
You brought the account to me. We can speak here without putting anyone's name on the board.
That is Oren's carving. Turn it over. The older name is beneath his paint.
That burial thread is mine. I thought it would quiet what they were carrying.
Someone bound it again with Vargan wire. I found the binding on the road.
The pack is dead. The people hiding this are alive.
Take your payment if you must. I need help I have no right to order.
I saw your account on the board. Rook has moved his bedding from the window.
People needed to know what was on their road.
Yes. And the people who can explain it need a way to survive being known.
Then we do both. I will not leave the second part to a notice.
Keep the originals if you need to. We can work from the account you choose to share.
Oren painted over a refugee's token. Sella wanted the first name restored.
Someone alive left drag marks beside the creatures' tracks.
Then leaving now would leave a witness carrying something dangerous. I am asking you to stay.
Hold the door. Elna is bringing broth, and I have both hands occupied.
Toma's daughter has a fever. The draught works. The roots it needs grow in the old ash beds.
Does Toma know where it comes from?
He knows I can bring the fever down. I have let him think that was the only fact that mattered.
Sella bought salve for Oren's hands. Too much carving. I have one jar she never collected.
The clean roots take longer to steep. I keep a cold cloth ready between doses.
You did not make the fever disappear by closing the ash bed.
No. Who needs help while the new treatment catches up?
Toma. He has not slept. Bring him the broth before it cools.
The jars have their source written on them now. Two families refused. Three asked questions.
I treated all five. Consent would mean little if refusal meant I stopped caring.
What will you say at the assembly?
What I used. What I withheld. What I am changing.
The fever broke. Toma thanked me. I let him.
There is your immediate result. A child is breathing easier.
And the part he still cannot choose?
Still here. Under the label I have not written.
The wrapped core shifts toward the names in the book, not toward my instruments.
It is a memory, not a patient who can answer me. I will not call a useful response permission.
Study what is already exposed. Do not open another name without asking the family.
Say Oren's name at the old stones. Watch the roots before you move closer.
The oil shows where the memory is caught. It does not decide what you should do with it.
And breaking the vessel?
Stops that shape. The memory goes somewhere else. We can defend ourselves without pretending the aftermath is nothing.
The chapel register and the roots turned toward the same name.
Oren restored a name on his token. The road's concealment could not keep it disordered afterward.
That brought the creatures?
The tokens drew them. The failed binding left the memory loose. Read the register before you face what took it.
The south granary is open. Tell the guard the sick household goes first.
Your seal was wrapped around a child's token.
My men were sent to contain a breach. They came back with empty hands and fewer men.
I have grain for Greyfen. I do not have a road that will carry it safely.
And the people who know why?
Bring their account to the castle. I will show you what another winter requires.
The carts will move without a household seal. I have given the order.
My guards can keep a road open. They cannot make the people on it believe me.
Begin with the first job. The second takes longer.
You have read the renewal order. You have not watched a hungry house divide its last loaf.
I have watched people be told safety was inside a gate they could not enter.
Then come to the record hall. Argue where the figures are.
You got the cart moving? Good. I was about to sell him a very expensive push.
Bram fixed my axle twice. Charged me once. Claimed he could not afford to be seen with a grateful smuggler.
You knew the other two?
Sella asked about the old road. Oren asked whether the crows paid me to follow them.
The road bends where the old waystone says it should not. I have a map. I also have a room somebody can find.
They copied the map with my family mark still on it. A guard came to my door.
You needed a witness. You got a target as well.
I will keep a way out open.
That was meant to be the promise before you put my name up.
I copied the route without the houses. The families know who has the original.
I will tell the assembly what I saw. They do not need my grandmother's bedroom to believe it.
You choose what is yours to share.
There. A sentence I could get used to.
I can still walk the route. I will not make another map for you.
Destroying the copy kept Vargan from using it. It kept the next refugee from using it too.
I can carry the route in the record without your family mark.
Then learn it properly.
The guard asked where my grandmother lived. Said he was checking who deserved protection.
My family kept names because the shrine would not. That does not make us willing to be nailed to a board.
I promised to stay with the people carrying this.
Then stay where they can reach you. The false waystone is a good start.
Harl used to warm my shoes by the fire. Burned one once. Hid it for a week.
You can know that and still hear what I ask next.
His grave bell rings with the rope cut. He helped close Greyfen's gate in the war. I told our children he held it for their safety.
Did he ever speak about the people outside?
He would stop setting the table when it rained. Find what he left. Do not decide for me that love makes me unable to hear it.
I told the children he loved us. Then I told them who stood outside the gate.
My daughter asked if both were true. I said yes.
Will you speak at the assembly?
About what I know. His victims do not need me performing my grief over their names.
I put the bell in the drawer. It is quieter in there.
You offered me a gentler account. I heard what you left out.
The record remains.
Then leave it where the children can find it when they ask.
The children have the account. I will not read it in the square.
You may name what Harl did. You may not use my kitchen as proof I have forgiven it.
Your grief stays yours.
Keep the scrap. I can spare a hinge more easily than another cart stuck outside.
The forge still runs. If the road goes, every household will want a latch before they want a sword.
There are letters ground off this iron.
Refugee marks. I recognized them years ago. Told myself metal did not care who used it next.
Some of it is holding doors shut against the rain. You want it back, tell me what we put in its place.
The new nails carry the names where a hammer will not strike them away.
I am replacing one working piece at a time. Elna still has a door while I make the marker.
What did it cost?
Two contracts. A late night. Less than grinding those letters off cost somebody else.
The refugee marks face outward now. Nobody buys this stock without being told.
The tools stay useful. A share of each sale goes to replacement iron and the road record.
You will say that publicly?
I already wrote it above the price.
The marked stock is on the table, with the forge accounts beside it.
Anwen will keep it until the families decide. I work from new scrap now.
Is the forge closing?
Not if you stop talking and help carry the clean iron.
She is asleep. Speak low. Mira finally got the fever down.
My daughter was outside when the bandits came. The thing at the fold put itself between her and a blade.
And the missing sheep?
I fed it. Then I hid it. It started taking from the next field and I kept telling myself gratitude was different from a danger.
Read the boot marks with the tracks. I want the whole cause found, even the part that is mine.
The outer boundary is marked. My daughter knows the posts mean stop.
The creature follows the old protection path beyond the fields. I warned the neighbors this time.
A boundary only works if everyone knows where it is.
There is a watch at the fold and a warning on every gate.
I do not call it harmless. I call the neighbors before I feed it.
They get to change their minds.
Yes. Even when I wish they would not.
The fold is quiet. She keeps asking why the thing that protected her had to die.
I told her about the sheep. And that I hid it until there were no easy choices left.
Keep its protection in the account too.
The neighbors stopped asking. That is not the same as the danger ending.
I heard it at the next field last night. I will not tell you I was surprised.
Hold the gate. Hold the gate. The lantern is on the wrong side.
You are repeating one night. Can you tell me your name?
Len. Mother left the lantern. Hold the gate.
A fragment caught in an empty grave. Not a man who knows what happened afterward.
Len. The lantern is on the wrong side.
You have kept the account where a living hand can reach it. That is something the old oath would not allow.
The grain condition is broken. No one standing here has to promise you anything to eat.
I remember the gate shut. I remember the road hidden. I remember the soldiers entering. I will not tell you those were one man's act.
You have carried what they tried to bury. You should not have to carry what we do next.
Then let your next act belong to you. Not to fear of my antlers. Not to another hunger at the gate.
The copies survive. I will freely keep what we have recovered. I cannot swear for the people who refused.
One willing keeper of an account is enough to begin. Others may share that work. None may be given it by force.
Make the account public and I will leave its judgment with you. Release me quietly and preserve the record without opening every private memory.
Or carry the unresolved binding yourself. Or destroy me and lose what no copy holds.
Releasing you does not erase the house's crime. Protecting a family does not protect Edric from the record.
Then choose whose work begins when mine ends.
The ledger counts ash as fertilizer. The wagon totals match the refugee register.
Closing the mill stops the tainted channels. It also stops the flour coming through them.
Keep the ledger dry. We take a copy whatever happens to the wheel.
Then look at the sacks. Those are tomorrow's loaves. Closing a channel does not fill them.
Keep the blade lowered. Those armored remnants still answer the road command. I stationed them here; I answer for that.
I was on that road. The first winter I wore a captain's coat, I could still smell the man who wore it before me.
You put the bound dead back on watch.
The living left. I called this keeping the crossing safe. An old command is easy to use when you refuse to ask what keeps obeying it.
Halvern refused to close the retreat. They hanged him. I closed it after him.
Now you take grain from travelers and call it repayment.
I told the men those houses owed us. Then a boy came through carrying flour for his mother. I took that too.
Tell me about the order. Then we deal with what you did this week.
My men have the custody terms. No levy can take their children for what I ordered.
I will speak. I am not asking the account to wipe the road clean.
Then sign the part you know. Leave the rest for the people who lived it.
The camp is packing. The signed account stays with you.
My men leave their blades for the grain they took.
Leaving does not make the missing travelers someone else's problem.
Do not close it. There are still people on the road.
Sanctuary under the Vargan seal. Those were the words. They came because of the words.
What happened after you refused?
Rope. The yard. Dawn. Do not close it.
Dawn. That is where you end. You have never seen Edric's winter.
I was ordered to retreat from another road. There were people we had promised to escort. I went.
The report said we could not hold. It did not say how long I kept walking before I looked behind me. I never went back.
There are still people on the road.
The wax will not hold. They agreed to eat, Edric. They did not agree to carry the road.
I left civilians on a road after promising escort. I called it a retreat in my report. That part of my report was a lie.
Then do not ask us to sign yours because you finally stayed.
I will not. The copies are here. Read them. Ask me what I did. You need not put your names beneath mine.
Open the grain list first. Let the people at the back eat before anyone asks them to come forward.
Every household receives its allotment. No signature. My account comes afterward.
I left people behind under a retreat order. I stayed away and called it duty. That is my account before I ask for yours.
Then give people time to decide. A hand raised in relief is not an oath.
I grew the medicine in the ash bed. Families were not told.
Some choose it now. Others choose the clean roots. I still treat them.
The cure was real. So was the choice I kept from them.
The ash bed is closed. I will explain why the replacement takes longer.
There will be shortages. I will not hide them behind a clean label.
I can tell you where the road ran. I have removed the family homes from the copy.
My grandmother kept these names. She did not leave me permission to hand you every private part of her life.
The road is evidence. The addresses are not.
You have the route. You do not have my promise to stand in a rite.
A record is not a person agreeing. Keep that straight.
I resealed the book after the novice died. Every year afterward I called it care.
I was afraid. That explains what I did. It does not give the unnamed people back their years.
My confession is my own. No household has to follow it to receive grain.
The grain you saw outside is real. So is the road that killed the people sent to clear it.
I found the command ledger six years ago. I sealed it. I was afraid of what the houses here would become without Vargan protection.
You inherited the crime. Keeping its proof hidden was your choice.
Yes. And now those carts need guards who will stand when the road calls their dead by name. The renewal is the answer I have. I need the households to witness it before the grain moves.
People who must sign to feed their children cannot give you a free oath.
Then show me another way. Stand at the granary when the first cart fails to come. Do not leave me explaining principles to an empty bread queue.
I have withdrawn the household signatures. My officers have the same order.
I will testify without my seal. I will supply the road under the assembly's account.
Your title?
Not mine to shelter behind after this.
I will say what you make me say. Do not dress it as consent.
Your ledger is evidence. Your threatened words are not a new covenant.
At least we agree on the shape of what you are doing.
You have kept the account where a living hand can reach it. That is something the old oath would not allow.
The grain condition is broken. No one standing here has to promise you anything to eat.
I remember the gate shut. I remember the road hidden. I remember the soldiers entering. I will not tell you those were one man's act.
The copies survive. I will keep them. Some people said no when I asked them to stand beside me. Their answer stays no.
Then begin with your own hands. Do not fill the empty places with another person's vow.
Make the account public and I will leave its judgment with you. Release me quietly and preserve the record without opening every private memory.
Or carry the unresolved binding yourself. Or destroy me and lose what no copy holds.
Whatever I choose, the order stays in the book. Families still need a road home. Edric still has to answer.
Then choose whose work begins when mine ends.
These pages establish what we recovered. They do not promise for the people who could not come.
Leave room for what the Hart knows that our copies do not.
People to return to. Not just work to finish.
I used to say the shrine kept the dead quiet. It kept their names apart.

lines.text: Clean the rite and the danger moves out toward the wood. Open it and memory enters this place. Hold it shut and the next repair may tear it again.

lines.text: None of those asks the dead what they wanted. A living witness can freely take the work of keeping their account. Not the right to make them disappear.

lines.text: Oren said the name. Something opened. This is not him returned to answer us.
If we break it?
This vessel stops. Its memory disperses. If we keep it, we must stop treating every reaction as an invitation.
Or return the fragment where his name can hold it.
Yes. I can refine the oil whichever way you choose. I will not price a formula against a child's memory.
The creatures gathered what the road could no longer hide. The wire came later.
Vargan tried to contain the evidence.
Keep that fact. This fragment cannot tell us everything that happened.
Oren was making something someone had erased readable again.
Keeping this close gives me time. It also leaves everyone else waiting for an account.
Tor's hinge. Mira's jars. Somebody kept doing the work while I was away.
The people who died can be named. Where their grandchildren sleep is not the same fact.
Bram found the tokens in the repaired road. Sella brought one for a burial reading. Oren restored the first name beneath his paint.
The name loosened what the hidden road had kept disordered.
And my thread failed to contain it. Vargan's men came afterward for the tokens.
Now Edric wants those households at a renewal. No signature, no grain. Your copies will reach them before his guards do.
I carry an account from Greyfen's road.
Every token is to be brought inside. Those are my instructions, and I put my name to receiving them.
Then you had better let me show it.
You may still leave by the gate. The road must carry people as well as orders.
The empty sacks go left. The petitions go right. Do not mix them.
Why are household signatures beside grain allotments?
A supported household witnesses the renewal. Those are the terms.
And the household that will not sign? Does its sack stay on your left?
What were they sent to collect?
Painted tokens, according to the intake notice. Vale can show you the order. I won't fill its gaps with something I didn't see.
I have laid the uncut page under the lamp. You may read it. I have waited too long to say that.
Sanctuary was promised under the Vargan seal. The closure order followed on the same day.
You kept both?
In the same drawer. I dusted it every week and told people there was nothing to find. Put my name beside that.
Sit if your leg is hurting. Then tell me exactly what you found.
Your soldiers reclaimed the tokens after the road repairs.
I ordered containment. The repairs had exposed a cache the shrine could no longer quiet.
You also kept the ledger closed for six years.
Yes. Before you ask the next question, know that I have no smaller word for that.
The command survived without the names. The register has the names without the command.
Together they establish who did what. Copy the page before any choice about its seal.
The wheel has sunk to its hub. Rook braces the cart while the driver tries not to fall against it.
If you are hunting something expensive, consider this wheel. It has eaten my entire morning.
Move your hand from the spoke. I will take the weight.
Then Anwen gets the driver, and the sacks get through the gate. In that order.
The cart stands on dry boards. The driver has Anwen's cup between both hands.
Grain inside. Person inside. A profitable morning by standards I have apparently lowered.
Put the clean boards over the rut. Leave the marked pieces where we can read them.
Repair the route without burying what it exposed.
People can pass here. The evidence has not gone back under their wheels.
An order can move grain. It cannot make a hungry person's oath free.
You may put your hand to one of those without agreeing to stand before the Hart.
Then keep the names of helpers away from the renewal seal.
Practical help before an oath. Nobody has to become evidence to receive it.
A short ration is a cost. So is using tainted machinery. The ledger does not make either disappear.
Keep the record whatever method gets the flour through.
Clean repair takes time. For now, these sacks are what keeps the closure from becoming another barred gate.
It gets flour through today. It does not settle what went into the channels or the work of replacing them.
The accounts stay public. Repair is work that people can return to see.
Copies prove the crime. A new promise must belong to the person who makes it. No ration list can lend somebody else's consent.
Tell me what you found. If some of it is still unknown, say so.
The pack is dead. Here is what I could establish on the road.
Bram was still gripping the cart brake. His ledger's debts were crossed out.
Red thread bound the black feathers.
My knot. I tied that thread for Sella.
Oren's wooden crow had his name scraped away.
Vargan wire bound a name to the creatures. Someone tried to burn it off.
The drag marks were deliberate. Boots followed the pack's tracks.
Give me what you found, show the village, or keep it while we make copies. Do not fill the gaps for anyone.
A public account is not permission to speak for the people behind it.
I will stay. The payment ends the hunt. It does not settle what I now know.
I have a commitment to Vale. You need to know that before I offer you anything.
Then you have a conversation to have with her, not an answer to take from me. I won't be the quiet exception to your promise.
I have made a commitment to Mira. I cannot leave that outside this conversation.
Then don't. If that promise changes, she should hear it from you. I won't write myself into the space you leave unspoken.
A private thing, then. I can manage that.
No wager?
Not everything valuable belongs on a table. Terrible discovery. Keep it quiet.
I am glad you have someone to return to. Their life is not a reward for what you survived.
I know.
I thought you did. May the ordinary days be kind to you both. I won't make your news the village's.
I keep listening for the steward to tell me which part of this I am allowed to remember. It is an unpleasant habit to discover in yourself.
You could leave.
I could. First I want to put copies where the witnesses can reach them. I don't want to exchange his permission for yours.
I didn't mean it that way.
I believe you. I still need to say it.
The copied facts survived. Hiding the original left me answering questions I didn't choose. I need you to understand both things.
You could leave.
I could. First I want to put copies where the witnesses can reach them. I don't want to exchange his permission for yours.
I didn't mean it that way.
I believe you. I still need to say it.
I am staying until the copies are in their hands. We can disagree about the risk. We cannot build a life in which you decide what risks I am allowed.
I want a future with you in it. Not written for me. Not promised somewhere else as well.
No seal?
Our own words. And the right to speak again if the words stop being true.
The assembly has given its answer. It isn't the end of the work. It means I can finally choose which part is mine.
And the room with the window?
Still mine to find. I would like to open it before deciding what comes after.
The assembly has given its answer. It isn't the end of the work. It means I can finally choose which part is mine.
And the room with the window?
I would like to show you when I find it. Today, I would like you to stay beside me.
Because you want me here?
Because I want you here.
We said we would speak again if the words stopped being true. I'm listening.
Whatever this answer is, it won't rewrite the record, or what we were to each other.
A woman asked me to keep her statement, but not her address. Fold that leaf inward. The account stays readable; her door stays her own.
An omission in a truthful record.
A boundary supplied by its subject. I used to confuse those with omissions supplied by a lord.
Does she know the difference?
She made me read it back. Twice.
You wrote that you would ask whose safety a page changes. Here is someone who answered: keep her account, not her address.
An omission in a truthful record.
A boundary supplied by its subject. I used to confuse those with omissions supplied by a lord.
Does she know the difference?
She made me read it back. Twice.
Your letter asked who decides. In this case, the woman whose account it is. She asked me to keep her words, but not her address.
An omission in a truthful record.
A boundary supplied by its subject. I used to confuse those with omissions supplied by a lord.
Does she know the difference?
She made me read it back. Twice.
A room with a window I can open myself. That sounds smaller aloud than it did in my head.
Not from this side of the wall.
And work I chose, with people who can tell me no. I spent years being useful to the wrong silence.
Is there room in that picture for company?
There could be. But I won't mistake someone needing a ledger for someone wanting to know me.
I would like a life with you in it. But not one where we call a dangerous secret kindness because it keeps our supper quiet.
You kept a secret to keep people alive.
I did. And I have to answer for it. Privacy is not a licence to let the next household suffer.
You want a promise.
An answer. If we disagree, say so. The medicines are still here either way.
I heard the apology. I need to see who gets protected when the next hard choice comes. That isn't work I can do for you.
And until then?
We can talk. We can be kind. We cannot pretend the question went away.
You have done more than say you were sorry. A dangerous account is no longer being kept at someone else's expense.
It doesn't make the first answer right.
No. It gives me something besides that answer to trust. I would like to try again, slowly.
I want you in my life, Kael. Not as a debt for help, and not as a visitor who promises every door the same return.
And the work here?
Mine to choose. I am not asking you to carry me away from it. I'm asking whether we choose each other.
The last patient is resting. I can put this basket down now.
Shall I stay?
Yes. Because I want you here.
Come closer. No account to settle for a moment.

lines.text: Then say it plainly. I would rather hear the truth here than find it in somebody else's kindness.
Ending this doesn't undo what was good. It doesn't change who needs medicine either.
The damp stems need separating before they spoil the rest. Ordinary work. No one gets a song for it.
Perhaps a very short song.
You can make it up by the beds. Keep the dry bundles apart. Those are for the houses, not the shop.
Those will keep. Thank you. Most people offer to kill something when I ask for help.
I know a useful knot as well.
An alarming range of talents. Leave the bundles here. I'll take them round when the fever breaks.
One fever easing. One getting worse. Reports settle an account, not a bedside.
Do you ever leave the work?
Sometimes. Not because someone decides I have done enough for them.
I wasn't asking you to leave.
Good. Then ask me what I need, not when I'll be finished.
You know what fed those roots now. I won't pretend being kind to me makes that knowledge easier.
I didn't come to weigh you again.
Then stay a moment. Tell me something small.
I used to think a quiet house meant everyone had left.
Mine is quiet for perhaps ten minutes a day. I've grown rather fond of it.
I'd like to know those minutes.
As a friend, or something you should ask plainly?
Lost that leg at Three Marks. Well, lost the money for the carpenter. The leg followed out of sympathy.
You could stop wagering the furniture.
And leave the roof undefended? Brace the stool by the common table. I've a peg that almost fits.
Solid. There goes my last excuse for losing.
The cards were marked?
Stones. And no. I'm trying honesty. It leaves a man terribly exposed.
At least he'll stay seated.
Hold this flat while I seat the pin. Elna's door has been announcing her business to the whole street.
No mark on it?
A hinge doesn't need my name. It needs to open when her hands are full.
There. Hear anything?
Nothing.
Best thing a door can say.
You won't see it again.
I'll see her carrying the wash through it. That's enough.
The cloths need folding. Leave the names where they are. I have moved enough things out of sight.
You don't have to explain every fold.
No. But I am learning which things I do have to explain.
It is easier to keep a table than an account. I used to pretend they were the same work.
The names are still here.
Yes. Whatever you think of me, they stay.
A moment, hunter. Elna has hurt her ankle. She cannot reach the water behind that screen.
The cup is on the step. Leave it on the linen by her hand, if you would.
And that little coat on the bench belongs under the shelf. Oren will complain if I let the rain into his pockets.
Thank you for the water. Elna has agreed to rest a little longer.
Would you move that little coat under the shelf? Oren left it here this morning. He said he would be too hot.
You found a dry place for his coat. Thank you.
Elna needs the cup on the step. Leave it on the linen by her hand, if you would.
There. Close enough that she need not ask again.
Was Elna with the missing cart?
No. A fall on the south road. Not every hurt here is a sign, Kael. Some people only need water.
That is Oren's. Leave the pockets turned in; he keeps things in them.
Did you mend this?
He did. I threaded the needle. He would not let me do the rest.
Bram drove the cart. Sella took Oren beside her. He left this because the sun was out.
He said Greyfen would leave us hungry if we stopped taking what passed.
I cannot promise nobody will ask what you took. I can promise supper is not a reward for obeying him.
And if we speak?
Then you speak for yourselves. Lowering a weapon does not sign your name to anyone else's account.
Mind the corner. That sack has already had a worse journey than either of us.
The wheel will need lifting before it can turn.
It will. The flour needed feeding to people before it needed feeding to mud.
There. Something went where we said it would. I could get used to that.
The kitchen has the flour. The cart is lighter.
I've told them you did the heavy bit. Don't make me a liar by offering to do it all again.
Leave the peg proud. Someone will need to pull it out when the next flood comes.
You expect it to fail?
I expect someone to repair it. A thing can be well made without being the last thing anyone ever makes.
There. A road ought to carry the person using it. Start with that.
Water's still moving. Boards are still holding.
If you're looking for praise, ask the wheel. It made the most noise about it before.
Did anyone ask what they had to promise?
One woman did.
And?
I told her the basket was not a contract.
Tell her again tomorrow. People don't learn that sort of thing in one meal.
I thought writing them where everyone could see would make my hands stop shaking.
It made you begin.
Bram. Sella. Oren. I have practiced saying the names of the dead more often than I have spoken to the people who miss them.
We cannot promise every answer today.
We can promise this question will still be here tomorrow.
Tor has begun measuring timber. Rook is arguing about who gets the first load. Go help them make this more than my handwriting.
This copy names the offices, the orders and those who gave them. This other book belongs to the families.
Who can open it?
The people whose lives it holds. They may let someone else read. They may refuse.
Edric's order stays on the wall.
Yes. His privacy was never the thing we were protecting.
The living still need timber and flour. Tor is at the bench. There is a world outside these books.
The silence held through the night. I kept waking to make sure.
I felt the road when I woke. Not words. Weight.
Then we write the limits now, while people are grateful enough to forget them. You did not accept every order anyone might give you.
If I cannot keep it?
We meet again. We tell the truth about the cost. We do not turn your promise into an excuse to stop thinking.
Tor has a repair for you. Something ordinary. Let him do it.
Nothing answered when I rang the bell.
Were you hoping it would?
I don't know. That is the honest answer today.
There are things we can no longer ask. We must mark those gaps instead of filling them with convenient answers.
We keep what remains. And answer for what we chose.
Tor needs another pair of hands. The next repair cannot wait for us to feel certain.
The west field wants its gate. The kitchen wants its cart. The chapel wants a board large enough to accuse the whole county.
The chapel can have the offcuts.
Who decides whose repair comes first?
Today? The people standing here. Tomorrow we'll need something better than whoever shouts loudest.
Put that on Anwen's board.
Where does that go?
To someone who asked me not to tell everyone where it goes.
You can still count the flour without counting the family's grief.
Keeping a confidence used to mean hiding my own part. I'll have to learn the difference.
Ask whose safety the silence serves.
Sit. If you're going to stand watch, you can at least stop this buckle cutting your shoulder.
There are other repairs.
This is one of them.
Help isn't the same thing as taking your oath. We can carry supper without carrying the Hart.
Come back before it splits again. That is a request, not a sacred duty.
It got everywhere. Doesn't mean everything is ruined.
No. Doesn't mean it didn't cost anything either.
I cannot put it back.
I didn't ask you to. Hold this end.
Listen. I missed that. We can miss what was lost and still be glad to hear it.
A public promise has a place people can return to.
Will you be here when they arrive?
I said I would keep it.
They asked for a marker. Nothing more.
Then it can be nothing more.
How far does it follow you?
I will have to learn.
Then don't answer for all the years today.
Will it grow?
We can water it. We can come back.
You still have Oren's coat.
The cuff is stiff with mud. I keep folding that part underneath.
What happens if you wash it?
Then it's a clean coat. I know that, but I keep behaving as if I'll have sent him away a second time.
You kept the empty baskets?
For the next meals. One handle's nearly through, and the woman who carried it apologized to me.
For the handle?
For needing the basket. I started explaining why she needn't, then I fetched some twine.
You've rewritten the labels.
The first ones were tidy and small. Especially the word ash.
Too small to read?
No, small enough for me to hope they wouldn't. These are less tidy.
New labels?
For the clean roots. I found room to write every steeping time.
And the other jar?
Still the old label. I keep finding very necessary work on the other side of the table.
You reached for that empty space.
The old jar stood there for years. My hand gets ahead of me.
What brings it back?
The kettle; the clean roots need longer, so I watch them. Waiting turns out to be part of treating someone.
Bram charged you for only one axle.
The second repair was free if I held the wheel and stopped advising him.
Did you manage both?
The wheel stayed up. He took what victories he could.
Can I still ask about the road?
You can ask. If I say a place stays off the page, it stays off.
Even when the route passes it?
Especially then. A road goes past a great many doors it hasn't been invited through.
Can I still ask about the road?
Here, where I can see who's coming.
You used to answer with a joke.
I still have them. I'm saving the good ones for a room that doesn't feel like an address you've handed out.
Can I still ask about the road?
Ask where it goes. Don't ask me to draw the houses back in.
You remember them all?
The doors, mostly, and which ones opened. A blank sheet doesn't make that a blank part of my life.
What did you use to grind the marks away?
That stone. Still cuts.
Why keep it beside the named work?
So I have to reach past it. I said 'still useful' about the iron, too, and I don't want the words coming out before I've thought.
What did you use to grind the marks away?
That stone. Still cuts.
You still use it?
On an edge, not on a name. I can remember the difference without pretending I need a different stone.
What did you use to grind the marks away?
That stone. It wasn't in the bundle I handed over.
Forgotten?
No, the families decide what happens to their iron. This bit is mine to remember.
What was wrong with my grip?
You held the hammer as if the board might answer back.
I've worked with worse company.
Board's better company if you loosen your thumb. Head does the striking.
You keep turning the seal in your hand.
I used to do that while someone gave me a number. It made an answer wait until I was ready for it.
Does it help now?
No, I'm discovering how long a silence can be when nobody has to fill it for me.
You still have the seal.
You have the ledger. Must I empty my pockets for this conversation?
I asked about the seal.
It used to mean people waited for my answer. Now they watch for what I'll try to keep.
You've rubbed the edge of the seal smooth.
It was smooth before you arrived.
I didn't notice.
You were occupied with getting an answer out of me. This one, at least, I can give without your help.
You read their refusal?
Twice. First I looked for a sentence someone must have put in their mouths.
And the second?
I recognized the way they complain. I used to interrupt before they reached the point.
You read their refusal?
The copy with the homes left out. I noticed the gaps before I listened to the words.
Did the gaps change what they said?
No, they just left me fewer places to look instead.
The sanctuary order is copied. You don't have to give it again.
Sanctuary under the Vargan seal.
I have that line.
Do not close it. There are still people on the road.
I hear you.
Sella left her washing on the line. I brought it in before the rain.
We keep working. What else is there?

Tor rubs stone dust from his thumb. 'Every time I stopped, I thought of somebody without a marker. Then I started making mistakes in the names.'
Tor signs his answer. 'I would like to go home before the light goes. You can put that down too.'
Mira shakes the envelope once. 'That is the sound of next year, if we are careful. It is not very loud.'

captions.text: At the old river landing, Nessa, Elna and Toma prepare a kitchen and dry sleeping places. The households disagree about where food should be held, but nobody must give testimony to receive it.
A common kitchen saves fuel and concentrates work. Household distribution preserves independence but asks more of the carriers.
The crossing needs sound joints, measured landings and a watch that understands the current. A public bridge and an escorted ferry are both possible; neither maintains itself.
A repaired crossing stays open between patrols but needs watch and repairs. A ferry needs less timber, but people must wait for its crew and weather.
Anwen and Mira inspect an upland refuge while Vale separates the public account from private testimony. Beds, medicine and a dry shelf come before names in a book.
Distributed public copies resist a single keeper's failure. Protected custody limits exposure but depends on fewer people. Shelter is unconditional in either arrangement.

The community tests a meal round, a night alarm and a record handover. Merrow, Edric and any surviving, willing Senn answer for the powers they still hold. Kael can offer his own work, never somebody else's assent.
A rota is useful only while its keepers can refuse, rest and withdraw. Missing volunteers leave work unfinished; they do not lose food or shelter.

The households ask for a dry place to cook, a steady table and bowls that do not depend on a name in a ledger. Some want one warm hearth; others want to take their shares home. First make both arrangements possible. Then choose where the daily work will fall.

The requests pinned here concern beds, clean dressings and dry records. Public copies can show who gave orders without exposing the people who sought shelter. No private name is required to enter. Prepare the room before deciding who may hold its accounts.

The meeting has three practical questions: who can pass on the meal round, how will the watch answer an alarm, and who checks a copy when its keeper leaves? Test those arrangements first. Ask people for their own answers afterward. An empty shift is an honest result; an absent person has not agreed to anything.
The names entered here belong only to people who agreed. Each keeper may leave the work; the promise gives nobody the right to appoint a replacement in their silence.
Kael sets the record beside separate keys. Care, the road and the copies have different keepers. None can close the whole account, and none inherits another person's burden.
The Hart rests while the first willing watch begins. Kael takes his turn among the others. This arrangement will need meetings, spare hands and difficult answers long after tonight.

The water carrier's household and the sweeper's household have asked to leave the failing shelter for Hearthward. Kael reads their signed requests. Named companions travel only if they separately agreed; nobody else's silence becomes consent.

Kael unfastens the boundary stones. Their light goes out. Greyfen loses the old supernatural shelter, and the Hart withdraws with the complete account that no copy contains. The human orders, signatures and protected testimony remain intact.

The boundary will not rise again. The households wait with their belongings at Lantern Reach. Kael must lead them over the prepared passage and bring them to the dry refuge. Until they arrive, this choice is unfinished.

CONCORD
The willing keepers divide care, passage and memory. Their initial acceptance remains in the record, but their continuing obligations can be withdrawn in person. A withdrawal leaves a real vacancy: uncovered care and copying wait, and an unstaffed public crossing closes until a keeper freely returns. Food, shelter and a safe service footway remain available. Kael cannot assign a replacement or erase a refusal. Meetings and handovers take time; the arrangement protects no one from the work of keeping it voluntary.

OPEN ROAD
The territorial ward is dismantled. The dependent households who requested relocation cross the prepared route and reach Hearthward with their belongings and the recovered human evidence. Only named people who personally agreed relocate with them; everyone else's answer remains their own. Greyfen's supernatural shelter is gone, and access to the Hart's complete account is lost. The refuge has ordinary walls, beds and a human watch. Those who remain at the old home know its protection will not return. The copies preserve proven responsibility and private terms, without pretending to contain everything that was lost.
The two households bring their own belongings. Their signed request is for shelter at Hearthward, not a vow to Kael. Keep close as they cross; the final load includes the protected copies.
The households cross only while Kael stays with them. The unsafe water is not a substitute for the prepared bridge or ferry.
Both households and the last load are beyond the water. The human records stay sealed under their owners' terms. Follow the ordinary road to Hearthward and open the prepared sleeping places.

The households put down their belongings beside the dry beds. The copied evidence reaches its prepared shelves. The old ward and the Hart's complete account are gone; this home depends on ordinary repairs and a watch that people freely take.
Anwen checks the recorded answers against the current rota. Every withdrawal stays a vacancy. No household disappears from the meal list.
Beside the public account, the rota records the next handover. The protected pages remain sealed under their owners' terms.
The public rota leaves uncovered shifts visible. Food and shelter remain available to households whether or not a name appears beside a responsibility.
The copied orders stay open to scrutiny. Private statements stay under their owners' terms; the new arrangement does not release them into public custody.
Rook checks the marked strap before loading. Tor leaves the repair tools where the next willing worker can find them.
Repair tools wait beside a marked strap and a list of worn joints. The next willing worker can see both the task and the space left for weather.
An uncovered shift is still written as uncovered. An unsafe part of the route can close until someone freely takes the work; a promise cannot brace a rail.
At the landing, one worker finishes while another checks the route marks. The work has owners; the road does not have a new lord.
The public route marks name the next handover. Household shares are packed for people staying and people going on; neither choice appoints a keeper.
Uncovered shifts remain visible beside the agreed ones. The community has a way to ask for help, not a right to fill the spaces with other people's names.
Vale checks the sealed envelopes against their owners' instructions. The departure list records places needed, not testimony owed.
A public notice points toward the copied orders at Hearthward. Human records survive the departure. Nothing on the notice claims to contain the Hart's complete account.
Sealed statements remain subject to their owners' terms. The departure list records the places needed without demanding testimony from the people using them.
The straps are empty now. The households who requested relocation have reached their prepared beds; no departing name was added without its own agreement.
The households and their belongings have reached Hearthward over the prepared passage. The old walls remain without the supernatural shelter. Human watch and repairs must now keep the refuge safe.
The walls remain. A notice gives the refuge's location for anyone returning. The people who stay behind have not been entered into a promise to follow.
The boundary stones remain dark. At Hearthward, ordinary lanterns light the settled households. No return to Greyfen restores the old ward or the Hart's complete account.
The route marks continue toward the prepared refuge. An ordinary lantern identifies the next turn; no new oath binds the people travelling beneath it.
The copied human record can be carried and checked. The Hart's complete account was not copied, and the open road makes no claim to restore what was lost.
